auditVerdict: PASS FOR USER REVIEW — Sprint S14 Shareable calculator state for Date Difference & Age Calculator across EN, ES, DA (/age-calculator/, /es/age-calculator/, /da/age-calculator/) completed. Features implemented: 1) Explicit share action (#btn-share-age in action bar and #btn-share-result in result container) and live region (#age-share-feedback) across English, Spanish, and Danish with WCAG 2.2 AA focus-visible outline (2px solid #B04A45, 2px offset); 2) Compact versioned query schema (?v=1&from=YYYY-MM-DD&to=YYYY-MM-DD) storing strictly non-sensitive numeric ISO date strings; 3) Locale-aware state hydration on page load with date population, immediate calculation, and localized number separators / milestone labels; 4) Robust fail-safe fallback and error recovery for malformed/unsupported query strings (?v=999, invalid dates, inverted dates from > to) gracefully resetting without throwing exceptions or showing broken UI; 5) SEO invariant protection: clean canonical URLs preserved across EN, ES, and DA and dynamic insertion/update of <meta name="robots" content="noindex, follow"> on parameterized URLs; 6) No auto-share / no silent address bar mutation; 7) Telemetry integration via window.ACAnalytics for share_link_generated; 8) Full automated verification in tests/test_s14_shareable_date_difference.js (17/17 passing) and 29/29 master repository test suites passing (100%), including 21/21 Playwright visual regression snapshots. Sitemap synchronized (441 URLs), ADR-053 recorded in .ai-memory/DECISIONS.md, and G1-G15 release gate evidence prepended to docs/growth/91-TEST-EVIDENCE-AND-RELEASE-GATES.md.
warningsRecorded: Loan Term Unit Toggle: Clarification that 8.58% nominal APR / 8.93% EAR in fixture documentation corresponds to a 36-year (432-month) loan input. When '#term-unit-mos' is selected, 36 months correctly yields 10.55% nominal APR / 11.08% EAR. Both modes execute with 100% mathematical precision.

Non-Latin-1 Characters in jsPDF: All supported platform languages (EN, ES, DA) and currency symbols (€, £, kr.) are fully preserved in Latin-1 / WinAnsi range; non-Latin-1 Unicode characters are safely mapped to '?' to prevent jsPDF Helvetica Type 1 crashes. Future expansion into non-Latin locales would require custom embedded TTF fonts.
